cards.body: AI 추천 뉴스 “사업이 우선” 지분 희석 감수한 이해진…네이버, 승부수 던졌다 [정지은의 테크킥] 네이버, 엔비디아 유증 실시 공시 엔비디아, 지분 4.54% 확보 다음달 27일 네이버 3대 주주로 이해진 지분율 4.03%→3.84% 엔비디아 자본·GPU 공급망 활용 글로벌 AI 팩토리 사업 본격화 엔비디아가 다음달 27일 네이버의 3대 주주에 오른다. 네이버와 엔비디아, 대체자산운용사 브룩필드가 손잡고 추진하는 ‘글로벌 인공지능(AI) 팩토리’ 구축 사업이 본격화한다. 이해진 네이버 이사회 의장이 지분율 희석을 감수하면서 글로벌 AI 시장에서 경쟁력을 확보하기 위한 승부수를 던졌다는 평가가 나온다. ○다음달 6일 유상증자 마무리 네이버는 엔비디아를 대상으로 10억달러 규모의 제3자 배정 유상증자를 실시한다고 30일 공시했다. 다음달 3일 최종 발행 주식 수를 확정하고 6일 납입을 완료할 예정이다. 신주 발행 예정일은 다음달 27일이다. 엔비디아는 다음달 27일 신주 724만1564주를 취득해 네이버 지분 4.54%를 확보한다. 국민연금공단과 블랙록에 이어 3대 주주에 오르는 것이다. 네이버가 제3자 배정 유상증자에 나선 것은 2008년 코스피 이전 상장 이후 처음이다. 이번 투자로 네이버의 주요 주주 구성에도 변화가 생긴다. 올해 8월 기준 네이버의 최대 주주는 지분 9.49%를 보유한 국민연금공단이다. 블랙록(7.31%)과 이해진 의장(4.03%)이 뒤를 잇는다. 다음달 6일 엔비디아가 지분 4.54%를 확보하면 이 의장의 지분율은 3.84%로 낮아질 전망이다. 투자은행(IB) 업계 관계자는 “이 의장이 지분율 희석까지 감수하면서 엔비디아를 3대 주주로 받아들인 것은 과감한 결단으로 보인다”고 말했다. 단기적인 지분 이해관계보다 글로벌 빅테크와 경쟁할 수 있는 사업 기반을 확보하는 데 무게를 뒀다는 분석이다. 갈수록 격화하는 글로벌 AI 경쟁에서 살아남기 위한 전략적 선택이라는 평가도 나온다. ○“사업이 우선…지분 중요하지 않다” 이 의장은 과거에도 사업 확장을 위해서라면 자신의 지분율 유지에 연연하지 않겠다는 뜻을 밝혀왔다. 1999년 네이버 창립 이후 주요 사업 변곡점을 거칠 때마다 지분율이 낮아졌다. 한게임과 합병해 NHN이 출범한 2000년 이 의장의 지분율은 12.13%였다. 코스닥 상장 시점인 2002년에는 7.82%로 낮아졌다. 이듬해에는 기업공개(IPO) 과정에서 분쟁을 겪은 새롬기술에 개인 주식을 매도하기로 한 약속을 이행하면서 지분율이 6%대로 떨어졌다. 2008년 코스피 이전 상장 당시 이 의장의 지분율은 5.10%까지 낮아졌다. NHN에서 분할해 네이버가 출범한 2013년에는 4%대로 내려왔다. 이 의장은 지난해 11월 두나무와 네이버파이낸셜의 주식 교환을 통한 기업 결합을 발표하는 기자간담회에서도 지분율 감소를 우려하지 않느냐는 질문에 “사업이 우선이지 제 지분은 중요하지 않다”며 “지분은 중요한 고려 대상이 늘 아니었다”고 강조했다. 이번 엔비디아의 지분 투자는 이 의장의 지분율 감소를 넘어 네이버가 글로벌 AI 인프라 사업으로 영역을 넓히는 계기로 봐야 한다는 게 업계의 분석이다. AI 경쟁력을 확보하려면 막대한 자본을 바탕으로 고성능 반도체와 컴퓨팅 인프라를 확보하고, 이를 활용할 기술과 운영 역량을 갖추는 것이 중요하기 때문이다. 업계 관계자는 “AI 시장은 일부 글로벌 빅테크가 막대한 자본력을 앞세워 컴퓨팅 인프라와 핵심 기술 경쟁을 주도하는 양상으로 치닫고 있다”며 “네이버가 글로벌 AI 시장에서 경쟁력을 확보하기 위해 엔비디아와 두터운 관계를 쌓은 것으로 풀이된다”고 말했다. 업계에서는 엔비디아와의 자본·사업 협력이 네이버의 AI 경쟁력을 끌어올리는 계기가 될 것으로 보고 있다. 네이버가 기대할 수 있는 효과는 그래픽처리장치(GPU) 확보에 그치지 않는다. 엔비디아와의 협력 관계를 바탕으로 각국 정부와 기업이 자체 AI 역량을 확보하기 위해 추진하는 ‘소버린 AI’ 사업에도 참여 기회를 넓힐 수 있다. 네이버의 소프트웨어와 플랫폼, 데이터센터 운영 역량을 엔비디아의 AI 반도체 및 기술 생태계와 결합해 글로벌 AI 인프라 시장을 공략할 수 있다는 전망이다. 정지은 기자 jeong@hankyung.com

cards.body: Nvidia is reportedly facing questions from the United States Department of Justice over whether its purchase of Hugging Face will have an impact on competition in the growing AI space. Nvidia agreed to buy Hugging Face in September, paying almost $13 billion. Hugging Face offers an open-source platform for the hosting and testing of new AI models, and that appears to be behind the DOJ's concerns. Reuters reports that the department has made inquiries about how the Hugging Face deal could change the landscape for Nvidia's competitors. The move could be seen as a way for Nvidia to lock in a key distribution channel for its own products. Hugging Face also sells AI infrastructure. Nvidia has declined to comment on the story. At home, the DOJ has also looked into Nvidia's purchase of SchedMD, a company whose software is used to run supercomputers that have ties to national security. Nvidia promised to continue to support the software as part of a larger three-year investigation into its conduct. Officials have also considered whether Nvidia dangled a larger allocation of its AI chips in front of customers who also purchased its networking hardware as well as Groq chips — Nvidia bought Groq for $20 billion in December of 2025. The deal included the acquihires of key members of the AI chip startup's team, including its CEO. As for Hugging Face, Nvidia has similarly confirmed that it will continue to support a range of chip and AI providers once the buyout completes. It's expected that Hugging Face will officially become part of Nvidia in the first half of 2027.

cards.body: Anthropic spent less than a third of its $8.9 billion first-half compute bill on serving customers, with most of the rest going into training, research, and running Claude internally, its S-1 filing shows. It has meanwhile signed up for hundreds of billions of dollars more in TPU and GPU capacity. By our math, it has meanwhile signed up for roughly $800 billion more in TPU and GPU capacity, and revenue per compute dollar jumped from $0.40 in Q1 2025 to $2.08 in Q2 2026, which the company links to capacity purchased 12–18 months ahead. Anthropic’s IPO is likely to beat that of rival OpenAI, which filed confidentially before CEO Sam Altman said its own won’t come this year, amid widespread doubts about an AI bubble. Whether AI labs can cover what it costs to serve their models is an open question. Anthropic appears to do so easily: it spent $2.4 billion serving customers in the first half of the year, versus $16.3 billion in revenue. Paying for what it has on order is more difficult. Its five compute deals with the biggest stated amounts would cost an estimated $103 billion a year on average once delivered, more than twice its revenue at Q2’s pace of about $46 billion a year. The company also warns that margins may compress as new hardware lands ahead of the revenue it will support. The company has three main costs: the cost of revenue, which is the inference cost of running Claude for paying customers; R&D, which is mostly compute for training and research into new models plus any internal use; and sales and marketing, which covers the cut taken by channel partners and cloud platform resellers. Comparing the first half of last year to this year’s, cost of revenue is up about 2.3x, but with revenue up 14x, that means Anthropic keeps an estimated 85 cents for every dollar after serving costs, up from just 12 cents. cards.body: Microsoft believes its data centers can last for up to 25 years. The company revealed in its Q1 2027 earnings call that it is extending the expected useful life of office buildings and data centers in its estate from 15 to 25 years. CFO Amy Hood said this reflected Microsoft's "operating history and expected use of these assets.” It is thought Microsoft currently has access to some 12GW of data center capacity. CEO Satya Nadella told investors on the earnings call that his firm continues “to get more from the infrastructure we already have by optimizing across the data center design, silicon systems, software, and models.” He added: For example, we increased the throughput for Copilot workloads by over 50 percent quarter-over-quarter. We continue to scale our fleet with the latest innovations from Nvidia, AMD, alongside our own Maia systems.” Research from the Uptime Institute published in 2024 found that data centers typically operate for 10-15 years, with the average mean lifespan of a data center sitting at 11.3 years. Extending the useful life of data centers is also a handy accounting move for Microsoft, as it can spread the cost of multi-billion-dollar facilities over a longer time period. The quarter saw Microsoft disclose the revenue of its Azure cloud platform for the first time, revealing it generated $33.2 billion in revenue in the last quarter. The figure represents a 48 percent Year-on-Year (YoY) increase, and means Azure was responsible for 36 percent of the company’s revenue in the three months to the end of September. During the period, Microsoft brought 24 new data centers online, but the company also reported lower-than-expected capex because a number of deals with neoclouds have been delayed. Microsoft’s Agents and Infra division, which includes its Azure cloud platform and AI tools, made $76.8 billion, up 25 percent YoY. Microsoft introduced Agents and Infra as a business section in its reporting in September as part of a move towards "full transparency of quarterly revenue across each of our key businesses.” Nadella said: “We are building against a growing book of business with a fungible fleet that allows us to dynamically allocate capacity to the highest value opportunities across compute, data, Foundry [its AI developer platform], and [AI assistant] Copilot. “Accelerating demand led to us adding 24 new data centers across five continents this quarter. We are bringing capacity online faster, reducing dock-to-live times by about 20 percent quarter-over-quarter for new GB300s in our biggest regions, which make up the majority of the GPU deployments.” Microsoft capex for the quarter was $45.2 billion, lower than the expected $50.7 billion. It said this was a result of some of the companies it works with for AI cloud services failing to provide data center capacity on time. headlines.body: The past few quarters of hyperscaler earnings have been marked by ever-increasing capital expenditure forecasts as tech giants race to build out artificial intelligence infrastructure to meet what they describe as insatiable demand. At least for the moment, Microsoft and Alphabet are telling a slightly different story. In their earnings reports Wednesday, both companies shared capex figures that came up shy of analysts' estimates. Microsoft reduced its capex forecast for the year to $170 billion from $175 billion, and Alphabet held its guidance at $195 billion to $205 billion. The numbers suggest a slowdown is nowhere in sight, but they do represent another potential point of concern for the AI buildout. Shares of neoclouds CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN all dropped after the reports, as did Oracle, which is one of the biggest spenders on AI infrastructure. Microsoft CFO Amy Hood said on the software company's earnings call that third-party providers of graphics processing units had delays that will push out some available capacity until the first half of 2027. She didn't provide names, but Microsoft relies on CoreWeave, IREN and Nebius, among others. Anat Ashkenazi, Alphabet's finance chief, told analysts that outside computing power "came online only at the very end of Q3." Alphabet shares tumbled about 10% in extended trading as the company missed on earnings and revenue and reported negative free cash flow of more than $9 billion. Plenty of Alphabet shareholders remain faithful. "We are pleased with what we see and what we heard, and trust management's approach to their AI spending," Chris Ballard, managing director of Check Capital Management, wrote in an email to CNBC. Investors will get a final read on hyperscaler capex for the quarter when Amazon reports results after the close Thursday. In Meta's earnings report last week, the company said it expects full-year capex of $135 billion to $145 billion, raising the bottom of the range from $130 billion. Like with Alphabet, Meta shares sank as the company reported negative free cash flow. Delays from emerging neocloud partners have occurred before at Microsoft, but they're more critical now as Anthropic gets set to go public. Anthropic counts on infrastructure from Amazon, Google and Microsoft for much of its computing needs, alongside capacity from SpaceX, Lambda and Nscale, which filed to go public in September but hasn't updated its prospectus in weeks. At times this year, Anthropic's Claude assistant has been unavailable due to climbing demand. Rival OpenAI, which has said an initial public offering in 2027 is likely, is also in constant need of more capacity. One big challenge for the market is that the neoclouds require billions of dollars in outside capital to fuel their buildouts but don't have investment-grade credit ratings. headlines.body: A top executive of a Singapore AI cloud firm that was accused of illegally selling Nvidia chips to China could also have been a Chinese spy, anonymous sources told the New York Times. The executive, Alice Huang (or Huang Le), worked for Megaspeed and was photographed as one of multiple people hanging out with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during various business dinners in the Singapore region. U.S. intelligence agencies had been surveilling Alice Huang to learn more about her ties with China for about a year, the Times reports. The concern, sources said, was that Alice Huang had grown so close to Jensen Huang that she could have been gathering information about Nvidia’s plans and the CEO’s efforts to convince the Trump administration to allow it to ship more advanced technology to China. But an Nvidia spokesperson denied this, telling TechCrunch that the CEO’s relationship with the Megaspeed executive was the same as with any other regional customer. “Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a C.E.O.’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” the spokesperson said in an emailed statement. The company also said, “Our regional cloud customers receive ordinary business information — not sensitive NVIDIA trade secrets — and zero information relevant to national security.” In 2025, the Times reported that the Commerce Department had investigated Megaspeed over concerns that it was helping Chinese companies sidestep AI chip export regulations by reselling restricted chips to them. Alice Huang was said to be a top executive for the firm at the time.

headlines.body: An Nvidia spokesperson on Thursday pushed back on a New York Times report that detailed American intelligence agencies surveilling a person close to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang because they thought she could be a Chinese intelligence asset. According to the Times report, which cited people briefed on intelligence surveillance, Alice Huang, who is linked to the Singapore-based cloud Megaspeed, developed a close relationship with Nvidia's Jensen Huang. Intelligence agencies worried that she was a spy, helping the Chinese government gain information from Nvidia and Jensen Huang, and fretted that Nvidia's CEO had access to President Donald Trump. The Nvidia spokesperson pushed back on the story in a statement to CNBC, saying that Singapore-based Megaspeed is another one of the company's regional cloud customers, and that Jensen Huang's interactions with its officials are not unusual, because he speaks with thousands of customers every year. The spokesperson added that customers don't get access to Nvidia trade secrets or relevant national security information. The report also alleged that Megaspeed was previously suspected of helping companies evade U.S. export controls on Nvidia's AI chips, which aren't allowed to be shipped to China. Nvidia said that Megaspeed had already been investigated for evading export controls. "The diversion allegations against this regional cloud were thoroughly investigated and debunked last year," the spokesperson said in a statement. Nvidia implied that the U.S. government had not briefed Nvidia on Alice Huang. "We're confident that if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know," the spokesperson said. Nvidia has had to walk a tightrope in Washington as its AI chips have become a powerful tool for all AI developers and a bargaining chip in economic competition with China. Politicians and analysts say that Nvidia's AI chips could be used to create Chinese military AI models, or commercial AI models that could compete and eventually surpass American technology. As AI has become more important to the government, Nvidia's Huang has befriended Trump and has given pro-American speeches about building U.S. AI infrastructure. Huang has appeared with Trump at state dinners, AI summits, and international trips, all while pushing for certain Nvidia chips to get a green light to be shipped to China. Earlier this year the U.S. government cleared Nvidia's H200 chip to be shipped to China, but Chinese regulators prevented their imports. H200s are Nvidia's Hopper generation chip, not the current faster Blackwell generation currently used by American AI developers. The Nvidia spokesperson said the Chinese government is not looking for Nvidia products from regional clouds like Megaspeed. "Instead, the PRC government blocked U.S. AI chips, protecting its own industry and resulting in the largest write-offs in U.S. tech history," the Nvidia spokesperson said. headlines.body: Donald Trump apparently is so aligned with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang—who has become the president’s key advisor on AI —that he ignored intelligence indicating that Huang was the target of a “Chinese spy plot,” and did so partly to protect Nvidia’s stock. The New York Times spoke with people briefed on US intelligence agencies’ surveillance and granted them anonymity to discuss findings drawn from “classified intelligence.” According to sources, about a year ago, Trump was briefed that “Beijing was getting reports from someone with direct access” to Huang. That “someone” was Alice Huang, or Huang Le, a Chinese citizen and former top executive at a Singapore cloud company called Megaspeed. According to sources, the US had already suspected that Alice Huang—who is not related to Jensen Huang—was helping China evade export controls to gain access to high-end Nvidia chips through Megaspeed. But it alarmed investigators to discover that she may have used her role at Megaspeed to gain direct access to Jensen Huang. It’s now believed she may have leveraged that closeness to feed China intel not only on one of America’s leading AI companies, but also to influence Trump’s thinking on AI. headlines.body: 테슬라가 핵심 자율주행 소프트웨어인 FSD(Full Self-Driving) 이용자를 늘리는 가운데 현대자동차그룹과 제너럴모터스(GM)가 인공지능(AI)과 데이터 경쟁력을 앞세워 추격에 나섰다. 양사가 자율주행 기능 양산을 목표로 한 2028년에는 테슬라 추격과 함께 현대차·GM 간 경쟁도 본격화할 전망이다. 제너럴모터스(GM)과 현대차그룹이 테슬라 중심의 글로벌 자율주행 시장에 도전장을 던졌다. 테슬라가 자율주행 소프트웨어인 FSD(Full Self-Driving) 이용자를 170만명 넘게 끌어모으며 앞서가자, GM과 현대차그룹이 인공지능(AI)과 데이터 역량을 전면에 내세워 2028년 양산 결전을 선언한 것이다. 테슬라가 최근 공개한 2026년 3분기 실적 자료에 따르면 글로벌 FSD 활성 구독·계약은 174만건으로 전년 동기(104만 건) 대비 67% 증가했다. 카메라로 차량·보행자·차선·교통표지 등을 인식하고 신경망 기반 AI로 주행 경로와 조향·가감속을 판단하는 FSD로 자율주행 생태계를 빠르게 잠식하고 있는 것이다. 다만 운전자가 주행 상황을 지속적으로 감독해야 하는 점은 보완점으로 꼽힌다. 악천후 시 시야 미확보 등으로 미국 도로교통안전국(NHTSA)이 320만 대에 달하는 차량의 안전성 조사에 착수하는 등 안전성 검증 과제도 안고 있다 이에 반해 GM과 현대차그룹은 실도로 데이터와 예외 상황을 활용해 AI를 고도화하며 테슬라 추격에 나섰다. 우선 GM은 데이터 물량전을 통해 고속도로 자율주행 기능 도입을 선언했다. 관련해 GM은 지난 21일 미국 뉴욕에서 개최한 ‘GM 포워드(GM Forward)’ 행사에서 전용 데이터 수집 차량 수백대를 통해 매월 약 100만마일(약 160만㎞)의 다중 센서 데이터를 확보하고 있다고 발표했다. 특히 가상 환경에서는 하루 30억마일 이상의 주행 데이터를 생성해 AI 학습에 활용한다. 연산 능력을 기존 대비 40배 높인 차세대 중앙 컴퓨팅 유닛(CCU)을 바탕으로, GM은 2028년 캐딜락 에스컬레이드 IQ에 운전자가 전방을 주시하지 않아도 되는 고속도로 ‘아이즈오프(eyes-off)’ 자율주행 기능을 탑재한 뒤 대형 트럭·SUV로 확대할 방침이다. 테슬라가 저렴한 카메라와 무선 업데이트(OTA)에 집중한다면 GM은 고가의 라이다·레이더를 결합한 센서 중복성을 앞세우는 식이다. 현대차그룹은 글로벌 반도체 공룡과의 협업과 자체 AI를 결한 ‘투트랙 전략’을 가동했다. 2028년 상반기 엔비디아 솔루션 기반 레벨 2+ 시스템을 양산차에 적용하고, 하반기에는 레벨 2++ 시스템을 선보인다. 2029년 하반기에는 자체 개발한 엔드투엔드(E2E) 방식의 ‘아트리아 AI’를 적용한 레벨 2++ 차량을 양산할 계획이다. 엔비디아 기반 기술로 양산 속도를 확보하되, 장기적으로는 핵심 SW 주도권을 내재화하겠다는 포석이다. 다만 현대차그룹의 레벨 2+·2++는 국제자동차기술자협회(SAE)의 공식 기준인 레벨 2와 달리 운전자 보조 기능을 고도화한 업체의 자체 기준이다. 아울러 현대차그룹은 현재 40대의 데이터 수집 차량을 주야간 운영하며 도로공사·악천후·급격한 차로 변경 등 ‘엣지 케이스(돌발 상황)’를 확보하고 있다. 확보한 데이터에서 난도가 높은 사례를 선별하는 ‘하드 이그잼플 마이닝’을 거쳐 AI를 학습시키고, 주행 상황을 3차원 가상 환경에서 검증한 뒤 개선 모델을 차량에 적용한다. 데이터 수집부터 학습·검증·적용까지 반복하는 ‘데이터 플라이휠’로 성능 개선 속도를 높인다는 구상이다. 업계에서는 2028년을 기점으로 현대차그룹과 GM 간의 추격 경쟁이 본격화할 것으로 보고 있다. 두 회사 모두 2028년 양산차에 자율주행 기능을 적용한다는 목표를 세운 데다, GM은 고속도로 ‘아이즈오프’ 기능을, 현대차그룹은 엔비디아 기반 시스템과 자체 AI를 앞세워 상용화에 나서기 때문이다. 업계 관계자는 “양사가 추진하고 있는 상용화 시점이 동일하다는 점에서 2028년을 전후로 자율주행 차량 경쟁이 본격화할 가능성이 있다”며 “다만 목표로 하는 기능과 운전자 개입 조건이 다른 만큼 실제 주행 성능과 안전성 검증 결과를 함께 살펴봐야 한다”고 말했다. 허인학 기자 ih.heo@chosunbiz.com
